- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The risks associated with getting a flu shot are usually very minimal, with mild side effects including soreness, redness, swelling at the injection site, fever, headache, or fatigue; severe allergic reactions are extremely rare.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is beneficial to get a flu shot annually because the flu virus can mutate and change each year, necessitating updates to the vaccine to protect against the latest strains.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Getting vaccinated can help reduce the risk of getting sick and spreading the virus, and symptoms are likely to be milder if the user does get the flu after vaccination.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is particularly important for people at higher risk of complications from the flu, such as young children, older adults, pregnant women, and those with underlying medical conditions, to get vaccinated.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user should discuss any concerns or questions about the flu shot with their healthcare provider for more personalized information.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Getting the flu shot is an effective way to protect oneself and others during flu season.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant emphasizes the importance of taking steps to protect health, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Flu shots typically become available in early fall (September or October), so planning ahead is advisable.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is important to get the right type of flu shot for the user's age and health condition, which is why consulting a healthcare provider is recommended.
